newsitem.title: ITALY: Eni says takes 35 pct stake in Albacom.
newsitem.headline: Eni says takes 35 pct stake in Albacom.

text.p: Italian energy group Eni said on Thursday it was taking a 35 percent stake in Albacom, a mobile phone operator owned by British Telecommunications Plc, Italy's Banca Nazionale del Lavoro and communications group Mediaset.
The company annouced the deal in a statement released ahead of a news conference. It did not say how much it paid for the stake.

The statement said that after the entry of Eni, BT and BNL will hold 45.5 percent of the group's capital through Albacom Holding, an investment vehicle. Mediaset will hold the remaining 19.5 directly.
Albacom Holding is 50.5 percent owned by BT and 49.5 percent by BNL. The investment vehicle in turn owns 2.4 percent of Albacom.
The precise stakes of BT and BNL in Albacom after the entry of Eni were not given, but Eni said it would now be the biggest shareholder.
As part of the deal, Albacom will take over the telecommunications infrastructure of Eni's Snam unit and will draw up a contract with Snam for the use of fibre optic cables.

It said investments of 550 billion lire were planned, of which 250 billion would be made in the first three years of activity, but the statement did not make clear whether the investments would be made solely by Eni.
The deal must now be cleared by the European Commission.
